PostgreSQL, also known as Postgres, is a free and open-source relational database management system emphasizing extensibility and SQL compliance. It is supported on all major operating systems and handles a range of workloads from single machines to data warehouses.

History

PostgreSQL evolved from the Ingres project at the University of California, Berkeley. The team released version 1 to a small number of users in June 1989. In 1996, the project was renamed to PostgreSQL to reflect its support for SQL. The first PostgreSQL release formed version 6.0 on January 29, 1997.
